question:
A manufacturing unit produces identical components using three machines $M_1$, $M_2$ and $M_3$. Machine $M_1$ produces 50% of the total components, $M_2$ produces 30%, and $M_3$ produces the remaining 20%. From past inspection records, 1% of the components produced by $M_1$, 2% produced by $M_2$, and 4% produced by $M_3$ are defective. A component is selected at random from the combined production and is found to be defective. Let $D$ denote the event that the selected component is defective. The inspection team wants to use the production proportions and defect rates to analyse the source of the defective component.

(a) Find the probability that a randomly selected component is both produced by $M_2$ and defective.

(b) Using total probability, calculate $P(D)$.

(c) Using Bayes’ theorem, determine $P(M_3|D)$.

(d) Compare $P(M_1|D)$ and $P(M_3|D)$ and identify which of these two machines is more likely to have produced the defective component.
explanation:
(a)
We have $P(M_2)=0.30$ and $P(D|M_2)=0.02$.
Therefore,
$$P(M_2\cap D)=P(M_2)P(D|M_2)$$
$$P(M_2\cap D)=0.30\times0.02=0.006$$
Hence, the required probability is $0.006$.

(b)
Using the theorem of total probability,
$$P(D)=P(M_1)P(D|M_1)+P(M_2)P(D|M_2)+P(M_3)P(D|M_3)$$
Substituting the given values,
$$P(D)=0.50\times0.01+0.30\times0.02+0.20\times0.04$$
$$P(D)=0.005+0.006+0.008=0.019$$
Thus, $P(D)=0.019=\frac{19}{1000}$.

(c)
By Bayes’ theorem,
$$P(M_3|D)=\frac{P(M_3)P(D|M_3)}{P(D)}$$
Therefore,
$$P(M_3|D)=\frac{0.20\times0.04}{0.019}=\frac{0.008}{0.019}=\frac{8}{19}$$
Hence, given that the component is defective, the probability that it was produced by $M_3$ is $\frac{8}{19}$.

(d)
By Bayes’ theorem,
$$P(M_1|D)=\frac{0.50\times0.01}{0.019}=\frac{0.005}{0.019}=\frac{5}{19}$$
From part (c),
$$P(M_3|D)=\frac{8}{19}$$
Since $\frac{8}{19}>\frac{5}{19}$, machine $M_3$ is more likely than $M_1$ to have produced the defective component. Although $M_3$ produces a smaller proportion of the total output, its higher defect rate makes its posterior probability larger.
